clue.text: Liberal in act of revolt turning away

indicators.note: in tells us the Liberal letter goes inside the word for an act of revolt

parts.note: a defection is a desertion of one's side, an act of revolt

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician's rebellion amounts to turning away from the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A deflection is a swerve or diversion from a course, the act of turning aside.

clue.text: Disturbance in the earth

definitions.meaning: a ..., as in 'kick up a ...', is a commotion or row
fine dry soil, the ground's powdery earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word joining the two definitions; the surface suggests an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust is a fuss or uproar in the phrase 'kick up a dust', and it is also powdered soil on the ground.

clue.text: Fussy female, a daughter needing particular food

parts.note: a dish is a particular food prepared for a meal

explanation.surface: A picky woman and her daughter each insist on special meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddish eater follows food crazes and is choosy, hence fussy about what is eaten.

clue.text: I must get away!

parts.note: read as the professional motto of an entertainer whose act is freeing himself from chains, locks and tanks

explanation.definitionFit: An escapologist is a performer like Houdini whose whole job is breaking free from restraints.

clue.text: Beaten and discarded outside front of hospital

indicators.note: outside says the word for discarded wraps around the letter taken from hospital

parts.note: trashed means thrown away, discarded

indicators.note: front of picks just the opening letter of the word hospital

explanation.surface: Someone was beaten and dumped near the hospital entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts TRASHED around H, the first letter of 'hospital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashed means soundly beaten, either physically or in a contest.

clue.text: Drunk used to being chucked out

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order, so the words used to are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk is used to being thrown out of pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' signals an anagram of USEDTO; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousted means expelled or removed from a place or position.

clue.text: Mark piece of clothing material that's been cut short

indicators.note: cut short tells us to remove the final letter of the garment word

parts.note: a scarf is a length of material worn as clothing around the neck

explanation.surface: Someone notices a mark on a fabric garment that has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last letter, F, from SCARF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting mark left on skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: It sounds like up-to-date cake ingredient

indicators.note: the clue openly says the word for up-to-date is to be heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: current means present-day or up-to-date

explanation.surface: A modern ingredient for a cake is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Currants are dried small grapes baked into fruit cakes and buns.

clue.text: Embarrassed about sweet course I consumed? One should have refused!

indicators.note: about means the word for embarrassed goes round the other pieces

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
pud is British slang for pudding, the dessert course
ate means consumed, as food

explanation.surface: A diner blushes after eating dessert and wishes they had said no to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the embarrassed colour around the pudding, I and the eating word, splitting it after its second letter. Pud is British slang for dessert. 'One should have' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate something is to reject or disown it, so repudiated means rejected.

clue.text: She may have dresses cut beguilingly

indicators.note: beguilingly suggests charm and deception, so the letters of dresses cut are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman wears alluringly cut dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beguilingly' signals an anagram of DRESSESCUT; 'may have' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductress is a woman who entices, so the female pronoun points to her.

clue.text: Excursion offers time to break out violently

parts.note: to rip is to tear or burst apart with force

explanation.surface: A trip offers a chance for time to explode in some wild way.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey or outing taken for pleasure.

clue.text: Leader of Brits, eminent fool looking silly in foreign provincial capital

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here from Brits
looking silly suggests letters out of their proper arrangement, so eminent fool is rearranged

explanation.surface: A British leader, a prominent fool, looks ridiculous in a regional capital abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' gives B from 'Brits'; 'looking silly' rearranges EMINENTFOOL to LOEMFONTEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloemfontein is the capital of South Africa's Free State province and the country's judicial capital.

clue.text: Drag a leg, drooping

definitions.meaning: to walk unevenly because of an injured leg

explanation.definitionFit: Limp as a verb means walk lamely, and as an adjective means slack or wilting.

clue.text: Musical ensemble getting theft forbidden in the auditorium

indicators.note: in the auditorium means as heard by an audience, so the words for theft and forbidden are spoken aloud

parts.note: steal is used as a noun for a theft, as in 'a steal'; banned means forbidden

explanation.surface: A band plays at a venue where stealing is prohibited.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel band is a Caribbean group of musicians playing pans made from oil drums.

clue.text: Team could be valiant losers, not half!

indicators.note: could be hints that the letters of the fodder might form something else when rearranged
not half means only half is used, the opening half of the word losers

explanation.surface: A football team that might prove brave losers, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' keeps LOS, the first half of 'losers'; 'could be' rearranges VALIANT + LOS. 'Not half!' is also British slang for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is a Premier League football club from Birmingham, England.

clue.text: Sun getting cooler according to German writer

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for sun (and Sunday)
chiller means a cooler, something that makes colder

explanation.surface: A German author predicts the sun will cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist of the late eighteenth century.

clue.text: In December that woman appears

indicators.note: In shows the name sits inside the run of letters across December that

explanation.surface: A certain woman turns up each December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' and 'appears' do surface work; the name runs across 'DecemBER THAt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a woman's given name, so it stands for an example of a woman.

clue.text: One shows you the minutes — ordinary writing, not typed

definitions.meaning: the clock pointer that indicates the minutes
writing by hand in full words

explanation.definitionFit: On a clock the minute hand is the longer pointer, and handwriting in full is called this as opposed to shorthand or print.

clue.text: Work with boxer leads to new attack

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a pug is a slang word for a pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: Working with a boxer leads to a fresh attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppugn is to call into question or assail, a dated word for challenging an argument.

clue.text: Grand manner making Greek god a pain

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and wild places
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A grand style turns a Greek deity into a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant style and confidence in how something is done.

clue.text: Fuse once awkwardly located outside residence

indicators.note: located outside says the rearranged letters sit around the home word
awkwardly suggests the letters of once are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: a flat is a residence, an apartment

explanation.surface: A fuse was once placed awkwardly outside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges ONCE into CONE, and 'located outside' splits that around the residence after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To conflate two things is to blend or merge them into one.

clue.text: An attendant collects an allowance for maintenance

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, also written a

indicators.note: collects means the attendant word gathers in the following letters

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A servant gathers money for someone's upkeep.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'An' gives just A, the article's short form; 'collects' then puts the second 'an' inside the attendant word.
explanation.definitionFit: An apanage is a grant of land or income given to royal children for their support.

clue.text: Commander meets lady (chirpy little creature)

parts.note: CIC is Commander-in-Chief
Ada is a woman's name, a lady

explanation.surface: A commander meets a cheerful little woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is an insect known for the loud chirping call of the males.

clue.text: Going away in vehicle, wanting to leave the wife

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: to leave says the letter for wife departs from the wanting word

parts.note: wishing means wanting

explanation.surface: A man drives off in a van, wanting to leave his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' drops W from the wanting word, leaving ISHING; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing means disappearing, departing from sight.

clue.text: Ham was brought aboard by him

definitions.text: Ham was brought aboard by him

parts.words: Ham was brought aboard by him
parts.note: Ham is not a cured meat for the ship's stores but one of the sons taken onto the Ark by their father in Genesis

explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the patriarch builds the Ark and brings his sons Shem, Ham and Japheth aboard.

clue.text: Lustful women getting escorted round

indicators.note: round says the escorted word goes around the letter for women

parts.note: led means guided or escorted

explanation.surface: Lecherous ladies are being shown around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd means crude and obscene in a sexual way, driven by lust.

clue.text: Lake? Pshaw, mon, it's this!

parts.note: och is a Scots exclamation of impatience, like pshaw, and mon is a Scottish address to a man

explanation.surface: A Scot scoffs, insisting that this is the right word for a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: a Scot dismissing 'lake' would say this word instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A loch is the Scottish word for a lake or sea inlet.

clue.text: Agrees gala can be arranged — opportunity for informal trade

indicators.note: can be arranged says the letters of agrees gala may be set in a different order

explanation.surface: A committee agrees a gala can be organised for casual selling.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage sale is a household's sale of second-hand goods from its home, an informal market.

clue.text: Declare or vacillate after losing wicket?

indicators.note: losing says the letter for wicket is dropped from the vacillating word

parts.note: to waver is to hesitate or vacillate
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket captain wonders whether to declare or hesitate after a wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes W from WAVER. 'Declare' is also a cricket term for ending an innings early, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or assert as true.

clue.text: Female boss in Berkshire town

parts.note: a maiden is a young woman, a female
the head is the boss of an organisation

explanation.surface: A woman is in charge in a town in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhead is a town on the Thames in the English county of Berkshire.
